result.summary: Adds structural inspection and safety analysis for descriptor-based multisig setups, alongside a new wallet RPC and expanded descriptor info. Core parses key occurrences and policy trees to verify whether a descriptor matches a recognized k-of-n multisig format without unintended spend paths or duplicate signers. A new `analyzedescriptor` wallet RPC and a `verbose` option on `getdescriptorinfo` expose these checks, identify which keys belong to the active wallet, and report whether the wallet can sign.
result.problem: When participants join a multisig setup, they must verify that the descriptor received from a coordinator enforces the agreed k-of-n policy, contains their own key, and generates identical addresses. Core currently provides no inspection of descriptor spend policies, forcing tools and wizards to parse descriptor strings manually and risking unnoticed vulnerabilities like repeated keys that lower effective signing thresholds.
evidence: PR description: "Before importing a multisig descriptor received from a coordinator, each participant needs to check that it is the setup they agreed on: a k-of-n where any k cosigners can spend and nothing else can, that their own key is in it, and that they all derived the same first address. Today nothing in Core reports what a descriptor commits to, so tools had to parse the descriptor string by hand, as the multisig wizard in #36325 (now closed) did."

Commit e14990c876: "Two cosigner slots are the same holder if they share a root key, or derive the same key at the first address (an xpub and its own child). Core accepts such descriptors, and fewer signers than the threshold can spend from them."
Linked tracking issue #35645 for native multisig setup workflows.
result.scope_notes: Stacked on PR #35918 (commits 1-3). Commits 4-7 adapt external inspection commits from contributor w0xlt, commit 11 is a move-only refactor into a shared RPC utility file, and commits 8-12 add the analysis engine and RPC endpoints.
result.card: Adds policy inspection and multisig safety analysis for output descriptors via AnalyzeDescriptor, a verbose option for getdescriptorinfo, and a new analyzedescriptor wallet RPC. Participants in multisig setups currently lack a way to verify via Core that a coordinator-supplied descriptor strictly enforces their agreed k-of-n policy without trapdoors such as repeated cosigners or spendable Taproot internal keys. The new endpoints report recognized setups, policy issues, which keys belong to the local wallet, signing capability, and the first receive address. Depends on PR #35918 and unblocks multisig coordinator tooling tracked in issue #35645.
uncertainties: Diff was omitted from the prompt, so validation relies entirely on PR description, commit messages, and metadata.

risk.why: Flaws in descriptor policy analysis or key matching could misinform users about whether a coordinator descriptor is safe or whether their wallet can participate in signing.
